questions.problem: Express ${cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{5})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{5})$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{2\pi }{5}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{5})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{5}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{2\pi }{5}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{4\pi }{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that our expression is a perfect square that can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{4}⁡({15}^{∘})-2{cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}){sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})+{sin}^{4}⁡({15}^{∘}) & ={({cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}))}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={15}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {15}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({30}^{∘}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{({cos}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({15}^{∘}))}^{2} & ={(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}=\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Express $\cos^2{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)} - \sin^2{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{24}\right)}$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x
$$

Substituting $x={\dfrac{\pi}{24}}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24})-{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{24}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{24}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{12}).\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x
$$

Substituting $x={22.5^\circ}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡({22.5}^{∘})-{sin}^{2}⁡({22.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {22.5}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y) = \cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y
$$

  

Substituting $y={\color{blue}x}$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies to

$$
\cos 2x = \cos^2 {x}  - \sin^2 {x}.
$$

This is called the **double-angle formula for cosine**.

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y) = \cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y
$$

  

Substituting $y={\color{blue}x}$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies to

$$
\cos 2x = \cos^2 {x}  - \sin^2 {x}.
$$

This is called the **double-angle formula for cosine**.

tutorials.name: Alternative Forms of the Double-Angle Formula for Cosine
tutorials.problem:
It's possible to write the double angle formula for cosine in two alternative forms.

From the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2{x}+\cos^2{x}=1,$ we obtain $\cos^2{x}=1-\sin^2{x}.$
Substituting this into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =(1-{sin}^{2}⁡x)-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives an alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine. We'll restate it below:

$$
\cos{2x} =1 - 2\sin^2{x}
$$

Similarly, from the same Pythagorean identity, we obtain that $\sin^2{x}=1-\cos^2{x}.$ Substituting into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡x-(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is another alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos{2x} =2\cos^2{x}-1
$$
